cards.claim: Optimal hyperparameters change substantially with training horizon (overtraining factor)
cards.conditions: Multiple optimizers (AdamW, Muon, SOAP, ADANA), models 51M–253M parameters, OT factors 1x–256x, base learning rate swept at every setting
cards.effect: Relative optimizer performance and optimal hyperparameters vary substantially—not constant across horizons
cards.evidence: Empirical study across model scales and overtraining factors
cards.quote: relative optimizer performance and optimal hyperparameters change substantially with training horizon

cards.claim: Preferred learning rate schedule reverses across the overtraining axis
cards.conditions: Same study setup: multiple optimizers, models 51M–253M, OT factors 1x–256x
cards.effect: Complete inversion of which schedule is optimal at different training horizons
cards.evidence: Empirical observation across the measured overtraining range
cards.quote: The preferred learning rate schedule can reverse across the overtraining axis

cards.claim: Best weight decay coefficient scales approximately as sqrt(OT)
cards.conditions: Measured across multiple optimizers, OT factors 1x–256x
cards.effect: Weight decay should increase as the square root of the overtraining factor
cards.quote: the best weight decay coefficient scales approximately as sqrt(OT)

cards.claim: Longer training horizons generally favor longer fixed memory in the optimizer
cards.conditions: Study of memory-based optimizers (Muon, SOAP, ADANA) across OT factors 1x–256x
cards.effect: Momentum/memory window should increase as training horizon increases
cards.evidence: Empirical finding across optimizer variants and overtraining factors
cards.quote: longer horizons generally favor longer fixed memory

cards.claim: Log-time weight decay and momentum cooldown provide gains that compound as training increases
cards.conditions: ADANA optimizer, across increasing training horizons (1x to 256x OT)
cards.effect: Substantial and compounding accuracy/efficiency gains from these schedule modifications
cards.evidence: Empirical measurement across horizons; gains compound rather than stay constant
cards.quote: Log-time weight decay and momentum cooldown provide substantial gains for ADANA that compound as training increases

cards.claim: Muon provides roughly constant token-efficiency advantage over AdamW across measured range
cards.conditions: Muon vs. AdamW comparison, most of the measured range (models 51M–253M, OT 1x–256x)
cards.effect: Constant (not horizon-dependent) efficiency gain from using Muon
cards.evidence: Empirical measurement across the range; explicitly contrasted with ADANA's horizon-dependent advantage
cards.quote: Muon and SOAP instead provide roughly constant token-efficiency advantages over AdamW across most of the measured range
